newsitem.title: USA: Binks-Sames sees Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Binks-Sames sees Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: Binks-Sames Corp on Wednesday said it board approved a restructuring plan that result in a fiscal fourth-quarter charge and a loss for the fiscal year ended November 30.

Under the plan, the company will reduce its product lines and close a 650,000-square-foot plant in Franklin Park, a move that will affect 360 support and plant employees. The company said it expected to cut about 50 percent of the staff.
Binks-Sames said the plan was designed to reduce operating costs by about $15 million in 1997.

"To achieve the growth and profitability goals set by our board, we must rationalize our products, concentrate on our high-technology core competencies and close the plant, which has lost money for the past six years," President Doran Unschuld said in a statement.
"Nearly 60 percent of sheet metal products and 50 percent of standard spray equipment items will be dropped," he said.

Binks-Sames, which supplies spray finishing and coating equipment, said it would step up efforts to buy parts from outside suppliers and shift many services performed by its own employees to external providers.
Existing plants in Colorado, Canada, Australia, England and France will assume remaining production. The company, which will now employ about 1,200, said those facilities were profitable.
